findings.title: Async legacy writes use the request-scoped context and will be canceled when the HTTP handler returns
findings.body: In `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection` (lines 51, 110, 135, 163), the background goroutine derives its timeout context directly from the incoming request context `ctx` via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`. Because the method returns immediately after the unified `Storage` call completes, the HTTP server will finish the request and cancel `ctx`, which immediately cancels the derived context in the background goroutine and aborts the in-flight `Legacy` write. Use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before applying the timeout so the async legacy operation is not canceled by request completion.

findings.title: Data race on `obj` between async `Legacy.Create` and caller using returned object
findings.body: `Create` passes `obj` directly into the asynchronous `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` goroutine while simultaneously returning `created` (which in Kubernetes REST storage implementations is often the same pointer or shares underlying state with `obj`) to the caller for serialization and post-processing. If `Legacy.Create` or `createValidation` reads or mutates `obj` while the caller accesses it, a data race occurs. `obj` (or `created.DeepCopyObject()`) should be deep-copied before being passed to the background goroutine.

findings.title: Object `name` passed instead of `options.Kind` to `recordStorageDuration` in `Delete`
findings.body: On line 106, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the resource instance `name` instead of `options.Kind` for the `kind` metric label. This records the wrong label value and introduces unbounded label cardinality into the Prometheus metric (one time series per deleted object name). Also on line 97, `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` is called instead of `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`, dropping the `name`, `kind`, and `method` log fields from the context.

findings.title: Storage and legacy duration metrics are swapped in `Create`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection`
findings.body:
Several metric recording calls record against the wrong store:
- Line 45 (`Create`): when `d.Storage.Create` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- Line 129 (`Update`): when `d.Storage.Update` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- Line 166 (`DeleteCollection`): inside the async goroutine for `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`, `d.recordStorageDuration` is called instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`.
